title: Bound magic in multi-qubit systems
abstract: Magic captures nonstabilizerness, a resource required for quantum computational speedups. We prove the existence of multi-qubit nonstabilizer states from which no pure magic can be distilled, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. Such bound magic states have previously been only known to exist in odd Hilbert-space dimensions, where positivity of discrete Wigner functions can be used analogously to the positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion for bound entanglement. We introduce a PPT analogue for magic in multi-qubit systems that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. This enables the proof of multi-qubit bound magic and the explicit construction of bound magic states for $n \geq 3$ qubits.

bite.hook: Bound magic states exist in multi-qubit systems: nonstabilizer resources that cannot be distilled for quantum speedup.
tldr: Proved the existence of bound magic states in standard multi-qubit architectures for n ≥ 3 qubits.
Introduced a PPT-like criterion for multi-qubit magic closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations.
Showed these states possess nonstabilizerness yet cannot yield pure magic states under any stabilizer protocol.
bite.whyItMatters: Magic states provide the crucial fuel for fault-tolerant quantum computers. Proving that some magic is permanently locked away reveals fundamental limits on quantum resource purification.
bite.eli5: Some coal burns easily to power a steam engine, but some coal is trapped inside wet rock and can never be burned no matter how hard you dry it. Bound magic is quantum resource energy that is forever trapped and cannot be purified.

glossary.shortDef: A nonstabilizer quantum state required to achieve universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.
glossary.eli5Def: Special high-octane quantum states needed to make quantum computers perform complex calculations beyond classical capabilities.

glossary.shortDef: Quantum operations generated by Clifford gates that are efficiently simulable on classical computers.
glossary.eli5Def: Basic quantum computer moves that are neat and easy to correct, but simple enough that classical computers can simulate them.

glossary.shortDef: Nonstabilizer quantum states from which no pure magic state can be extracted via stabilizer operations.
glossary.eli5Def: Quantum states that have computational magic in them, but it is irreversibly trapped and cannot be distilled.

glossary.shortDef: Positive Partial Transpose test; an algebraic condition used to detect quantum entanglement.
glossary.eli5Def: A mathematical test on a quantum state to see whether it has strange non-classical links or unextractable entanglement.
